content: Alhandal was a term historically used in Arabian pharmacy to refer to the purgative extract derived from colocynth, also known as Bitter Cucumber (scientifically named Citrullus colocynthis). The Troches of Alhandal, or Trochisci Alhandalæ, were a type of medicinal lozenge or tablet that consisted of colocynth, bdellium (a resin obtained from certain trees), and gum tragacanth (a natural gum used as a binder or stabilizer). These troches were highly regarded for their effectiveness as purgatives and were employed in various medical situations to induce bowel movements or cleanse the digestive system. The term alhandal itself originates from the Arabic word handel or handhal, which was a name used to describe colocynth.
